steps.content: Romanesque Hall

The stele garden now looks starkly different than it did when you first came here. Most of the stelae have collapsed, and the white marble blocks scatter among the weeds. Some graves have cracked, revealing the coffins.
When you walk into the stele garden, a crow flutters its wings and flies away from a stele. You notice a bunch of black vines climbing on the stele, with a small yellow flower blooming on it.
What kind of flower is that?
Seeing the flower, Oak Casket's gaze sharpens. She squats down next to the vines and gently caresses the small flower.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Raven
You listen carefully, but the stele garden is like a frozen space, without even a whisper of wind.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This is an oak flower. Or rather, an oak flower that's been branded.
But these vines are not even branches of an oak.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This is the branding effect. These vines grew from an oak coffin, so its flower is a duplicate of an oak flower. The person buried under this stele was a gardener who was fond of plants.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: There is an oak tree behind the stele garden. Half of it was blown away by the explosion of the monastery, but it still survived.
Because of this gardener?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Yes, he cared for every plant within his sight and dreamed of living in a forest, even though he never saw a real forest in his life.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Before his death, he asked me not to use dried wood for his coffin. He wished to become one with these plants.
Did he die in this war as well?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: No... much earlier than that.
Oak Casket smiles gently.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He died in a gang fight.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He was the monastery's gardener. The monastery had some peaceful days until a gang threatened them and made the place their hideout for some big shot.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Soon, the fact that the big shot was hiding in the monastery was discovered. Other gangs besieged the monastery, and many people died in that siege.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: At that time... when I returned to the monastery... he was on his deathbed.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He was the first person I laid to rest.
Did he leave behind any regrets?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He was worried about that oak tree behind the monastery.
As dusk falls, you look toward the back of the stele garden in the twilight. There is nothing there, only vast and empty darkness in the distance.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It didn't survive the last war. But I kept part of it.
Oak Casket spreads her hand to reveal an acorn in her palm. She places the acorn next to the small flower, watching it.
You walk along the path of the stele garden, fixing the damaged tombstones along the way. Oak Casket seems to remember every tombstone owner and the locations of all tombstones and coffins.
A nearly worn-out hat sits on a tombstone. Oak Casket gently removes the hat and starts mending it.
Is this hat yours?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: No, it belonged to a little girl named Nasha. The one buried here was her best friend. That child was sickly her whole life. Nasha probably worried that she would catch a cold from the wind and rain here.
...Did the child die of illness?
Oak Casket shakes her head slightly.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The gang took her away. Two days after they brought her back, her mother found her in a reaction pool at the Drifter Camp. I made her a wig and a mask so that she could look like herself in departure.
Her gentle, sad gaze falls on the tombstone again, where the little girl's name is engraved, but the name has long since faded.
...What about Nasha? Hasn't she come to replace this hat? It looks... quite old.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: She can't come anymore.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: That's her tombstone.
Following Oak Casket's gaze, you see another newer tombstone behind the hat bearing Nasha's name and date of death.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: A conflict broke out when the Executive Committee came to clear the Mania contamination. An incendiary bomb hit her room.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The fire burned for three hours before it was extinguished. Nasha's family asked me to help find the remains in the ruins. When I got there, there was nothing but charred debris and ashes from the fire.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The fire swallowed the residential building. I heard cries from both adults and children. The firefighters were stuck outside the block. By the time they got in, the flames had reached the roof.
You can almost visualize the fire from Oak Casket's description. The sky is dyed red. The flames blend into the sunset, like a flock of bright red sparrows struggling to escape.

Not far from Nasha's tombstone, there is a cluster of dilapidated stelae. You stop there and find that the greater part of the nearest tombstone has been blasted away, leaving only a small broken stub. The ground has also been damaged, revealing half a medicine bottle shallowly buried in the soil.
Half of the glass bottle is shattered, spilling shiny buttons and broken glass bits all over the ground.
What is this?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Stars.
You remain silent, quietly waiting for Oak Casket's elaboration.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: His name was Humar. He was bullied from a young age for having white hair and skin. His mother gave birth to him in a basement and he was kept away from sunlight for many years.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: People told him that his mother went where the stars were, so he started collecting these stars. Later, someone told him that the Drifter Camp was in a high and starry place and that when the night was clear, you could even touch them, so he came. Only eight years old, he came carrying his only belongings.
She picks up the bottle and carefully puts the buttons back into the remaining half of the bottle.
There are so many buttons. He must have spent a long time collecting them.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I collected some for him, but he didn't want them. He only kept the ones he collected himself.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I still remember his expression at that time. He liked those buttons but couldn't accept them... His eyes were wide open. It was quite amusing.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He asked me where I got so many stars, so I took him where I found the buttons. The morgue in the monastery.
Then what happened next?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: After that, he became my playmate.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: When I was a child, I often went to the morgue by myself. It was the quietest place in the monastery. I brought him to the room, thinking it would scare him...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But he was just envious of me, for I could have such a big room all to myself... Oh dear.
Oak Casket lets out a soft gasp. You step forward to help steady the glass bottle, catching the stars almost spilling out.
Oak Casket's gaze travels from the glass bottle to you. The light from the bottle is reflected in her pupils, warming up her gaze as she looks at you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: One night, he appeared in the morgue again, but this time... he was unrecognizable.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: He was tricked into climbing a high-rise building in Syndicate to pick stars, and ended up falling.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: His final regret was only a bottle full of buttons.
Oak Casket rises and walks into the cluster of broken stelae.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Most of the people buried around here were from the monastery... These people fell into eternal slumber because of the living.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You see, the dead won't hurt you, only the living will.
Her tone is calm, as if she's merely stating an objective fact.

You want to object and tell her that's not true, that there are many trustworthy and good people among the living. But perhaps because the wind in the graveyard is too quiet, somehow you can't bring yourself to speak.
The two of you proceed in silence for a while until Oak Casket stops in front of a somewhat weathered tombstone. She stares at the stele for a long time without saying a word.
Whose tombstone is this?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I don't know.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: But what remains here... is the regret I cannot resolve.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I've resolved the regrets of the dead from all walks of life. Those who passed away in accidents, those who chose to go because they couldn't see hope...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Yet I've never truly understood the message the person lying beneath this tombstone has left me.
You reach out your hand toward Oak Casket.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I'm afraid it's difficult. She didn't leave much information.
Oak Casket is much gentler in the Romanesque Hall than in the interrogation room.
Give it a try.
This time there are two of us. We should be able to hear more.
She looks into your eyes, as if she's glimpsing through something you don't know. In the end, she takes off her gloves and covers your eyes.
The chill of Oak Casket's palms still remains over your eyes. Your vision is blank.
Gradually, a warm light arises, dispelling the chill in your eyes.
You find yourself in a meadow under the warm sunlight. It's a beautiful sunny day.
Perhaps because the tombstone has stood there for too long, you can't make out clearly what you're seeing. You can only vaguely see a girl reciting something under a tree.
Her voice is so soft that you can't hear what she's reciting. You turn to look at Oak Casket, who's also straining her ears to listen.
What is she reciting?
Oak Casket doesn't respond.
Meanwhile, the figure of an adult approaches and joins the girl in her recitation.
Like a melody, the peaceful and warm voice floats in the air with the sunlight. The light about the girl grows brighter and brighter.
Hardships... Traveler... Light...
These words somehow ring a bell.
Wanting to hear more clearly, you strain to step forward, but end up stepping into a sea of white light.
The two of you have returned to the stele.
The link of the shackles still remains, so you feel the repressed emotion from Oak Casket almost as soon as you come back.
Why? The sun was so warm and mellow.
Did you just see the same things as you had previously?
Before we came, we made an agreement that you would do your best to assist me.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: ...This time, I could hear her recitation.
You sense the emotion coming from the shackles, guiding Oak Casket.
The poem she recited... I only heard a few words, but I'm certain I've heard it somewhere before.
Do you remember?
Oak Casket falls silent again, but through the shackles, you can feel what she's feeling... Something like contempt or anger... Or perhaps... sadness.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Such a foolish and despicable poem...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I've forgotten about it.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Do I need to recall it, Chief?
Her tone is somewhat harsh, but you feel that her sadness outweighs her anger.
You don't want her to be stuck in this kind of pain, so you shake your head slightly.
You stand next to Oak Casket for a while until the emotion on the other end of the shackles subsides.
You said that everyone sleeping here was connected to the monastery.
Are there any other people from the monastery still alive? Or people related to the monastery. They may know something.
...If remembering will cause you pain, then let me find these answers.
After a moment of silence, Oak Casket finally answers you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: There's a doctor who's closely related to the monastery... but I'm not sure if he's still alive.
It's okay. Let's try to find him.
Before leaving the stele garden, you look back. The land where the oak tree once grew is empty.
There's still not a breath of wind in the stele garden. The tombstones are gray, just as those stars sealed in the glass jar are.
